perplex

per-PLEKS · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To perplex is to completely confuse or baffle someone, usually with something puzzling.

The disappearing-coin trick perplexed the entire birthday party, including the parents.

Example

The detective was perplexed by a locked-room murder scene that seemed to have no possible entry point for the killer.

Perplex fits a genuinely puzzling problem or mystery -- something with no obvious answer -- more than everyday confusion.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

baffle: To baffle is to defeat someone's understanding completely -- a baffling result makes no sense no matter how it is examined. To perplex is nearly as strong but points at the tangle: a perplexed person is caught among contradictory clues, still working through them.

stump: To stump is to stop someone cold: a question stumps you when you have no answer and nothing left to try. To perplex keeps you in motion -- a perplexed person is still testing ideas that keep failing. Stumped means out of ideas; perplexed means lost among them.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

illuminate: to make something clear and understandable

settle: to resolve a question definitively

Where it sits · how deep the confusion runs — puzzle → perplex → stupefy

puzzle vs. perplex: Puzzle is weaker than perplex: a single odd word choice might puzzle a reader briefly, but an argument that perplexes leaves them thoroughly and completely baffled.

stupefy vs. perplex: Stupefy is stronger than perplex: a perplexed student is still turning the problem over, while a stupefied one is too stunned and dazed to think at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — per-

prefix — per-: thoroughly, throughout (Latin per-)

root — -plex

root — -plex: woven, entangled (Latin plectere/plexus)

Put it together

Put it together: Perplex comes from Latin per- ("thoroughly") + plexus ("woven, entangled") -- literally something thoroughly tangled, which came to describe a mind tangled up in confusion.

Use the root in a new word: complex

Use the root in a new word: complex: A complex machine has so many interconnected moving parts that a single manual isn't enough to explain it.
